subject: Feature unitization & CAC payback — post-demo econ recap
messages:

Subject: Feature unitization & CAC payback — post-demo econ recap

Hi Dana — great conversation this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap and the numbers we discussed so we have alignment before I put a pilot SOW together:

1) Target feature scope (what we demonstrated)
   - Smart summarization + contextual suggestions inside clinician notes (single API endpoint, 1 request per note)

2) Consumption assumptions (what you said on the call)
   - Average tokens per request: ~650 (prompt + response)
   - Active users (clinicians) to pilot: 120 MAU initially, scale to 2,000 MAU in 12 months
   - Expected requests per active user per month: 40 (mix of short/long notes)
   - Monthly token volume: 650 * 40 * MAUs => ~3.12M tokens/mo (pilot: ~3.12M for 120 MAU -> 3.12M)

3) Budget and pricing signals you gave
   - Annual evaluation budget range: $30k–$80k for the first 12 months (pilot + early rollout)
   - Internal target: keep feature incremental cost < $/feature goal and CAC payback <= 9 months

4) Asks / next steps we agreed
   - Dana: confirm pilot MAU and whether procurement wants the SOW + MSA or a short-term eval first (you mentioned procurement prefers a 90-day pilot contract)
   - Logan: share a short econ breakdown with $/1M token scenarios, recommended pricing target per feature, and a CAC payback sensitivity table (attached).

I attached econ-scenario-v1.xlsx with a quick sensitivity grid (quantization + batching vs. $/1M tokens). I put a couple of illustrative price points but need your confirmation on the pilot MAU and procurement timeline to finalize.

If that matches what you heard, can we lock 2027-05-25 at 10:00am PT for a 30-minute pilot kickoff?

Thanks — Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: econ-scenario-v1.xlsx (xlsx), onepager-pricing-summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-19T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Feature unitization & CAC payback — econ breakdown (draft)

Marissa / Karthik — drafting the econ breakdown for Dana / HealthSync. Pulling the numbers into one place; please review the assumptions below and call out anything you disagree with before I send to procurement.

Assumptions (pilot, 90-day):
- Pilot MAU: 120 clinicians
- Requests per user / month: 40
- Tokens / request: 650 average
- Pilot monthly tokens: 120 * 40 * 650 = 3,120,000 tokens

Redwood cost assumptions (on-hosted, with conservative batching + int8 quantization):
- Baseline inference cost: $480 per 1M tokens (conservative)
- Optimized cost (aggressive batching + caching): $300 per 1M tokens

Economics (monthly pilot):
- Baseline monthly inference cost: 3.12M tokens * $480 / 1M = $1,497.60 -> round to $1,498
- Optimized monthly inference cost: 3.12M * $300 / 1M = $936

Convert to $/feature (per clinician per month) assuming 40 requests/mo:
- Baseline: $1,498 / 120 clinicians = $12.48 / clinician / month (inference cost) -> $0.312 / request
- Optimized: $936 / 120 = $7.80 / clinician / month -> $0.195 / request

Suggested pricing targets to hit finance payback / margin goals:
- If HealthSync wants payback <= 9 months and target gross margin on the feature >= 65%, then target monetization per clinician / month needs to be ~ $36–$40 (feature price), which implies $/1M tokens target <= $900 under current usage patterns.
- For 6-month payback and 70% margin, aim for $/1M tokens <= $700 and a feature price >= $42 / clinician / month.

CAC payback example (assumptions):
- CAC (average) allocated to feature: $120 per new clinician during rollout (sales + onboarding)
- Monthly contribution margin per clinician (feature price $36, margin 65%): $23.4/mo -> payback ~5.1 months
- With feature price $25 and margin 60% -> contribution $15 -> payback 8 months

Notes / asks before I send to Dana:
- Marissa: confirm we can commit to the optimized $/1M tokens target when we propose the pilot pricing (i.e., are we comfortable guaranteeing $700–$900 range for pilot SLA?)
- Karthik: any product constraints re: per-request token reductions (prompt engineering, shorter defaults) that materially change the token estimate?

Attachment: econ-scenario-v1.xlsx includes the above calc tab + a 3-point sensitivity on tokens/request (550/650/800) and $/1M tokens (300/480/900).

Thanks — Logan
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RE: Feature unitization & CAC payback — econ breakdown (draft)

Quick notes from product side — agree with the spreadsheet baseline, and a couple suggestions to tighten the tails:

1) Token reduction levers
   - Trimming system prompt by 60–80 tokens after pilot (safe optimization)
   - Enforcing a soft max response length that removes ~100 tokens on average for follow-ups
   - Local prefix caching for repeated context (expected 5–10% savings quickly)

2) Service-level cost tradeoffs
   - If we need sub-500ms p95 for clinician interactions, cost rises ~25% due to smaller batch windows — call that out as a premium tier.

3) Recommended offer structure for pilot
   - Option A (low risk): Flat pilot fee $12k for 90 days covering up to 12M tokens (simple for procurement; gives HealthSync predictability)
   - Option B (usage-aligned): $800 per 1M tokens + $3k onboarding fee (lower upfront, aligns with usage)

4) Marketing / CAC assumptions to include in the SOW
   - We assume onboarding to full clinician requires 2 touchpoints (CS + training) -> $120 CAC per clinician is conservative but reasonable for the vertical.

If we aim to show HealthSync a clear path to 6–9 month payback, Option B with a commitment band ($700–$900 / 1M tokens after the pilot) plus a $12k pilot credit for the first 90 days might be the simplest procurement-friendly approach.

I'll review the econ spreadsheet and send one small revision (token trimming scenario) — go ahead and send the draft to Dana with both options and the one-pager. I'll loop in infra if they push on low-latency SLA cost delta.

— Karthik

Subject: Pilot proposal & 2 pricing options for HealthSync (90-day)

Hi Dana — following up with a concise proposal based on yesterday's internal review. Attached is a one-pager and the econ workbook. Two pilot pricing options we recommend (pick the procurement-friendly one):

Option A — Predictable pilot (procurement-friendly)
- Flat fee: $12,000 for 90 days
- Covers up to 12M tokens (pilot expected at ~9.36M over 90 days if sustained usage)
- Includes basic support and one tuning cycle

Option B — Usage-aligned (lower upfront)
- $800 per 1M tokens during pilot + $3,000 onboarding fee
- Post-pilot committed band discussion: target $700–$900 per 1M tokens depending on SLA and batch/caching commitments

Why these options
- Gives you predictable procurement-friendly terms (A) or a usage-linked approach (B). Either path can hit your 6–9 month payback target depending on feature price and activation. See attached onepager-pricing-summary.pdf and the econ-scenario-v1.xlsx for the detailed sensitivity.

Next steps
- Please confirm which option procurement prefers. If Option A, a short SOW + PO is sufficient; if Option B, we can send a lean SOW + DocuSign link for the $3k onboarding + usage terms.
- Can we schedule the pilot kickoff for Tue 2027-05-25 at 10:00am PT?

Links & attachments:
- Econ workbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-econ-scenarios
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/HS-2027-0421
- DocuSign (if usage-aligned SOW chosen): https://www.docusign.com/link/pilot-sow-HS-2027

If you want a one-line pricing commitment to show procurement right away: we can say "Pilot Option B: $800 / 1M tokens for 90 days with a post-pilot target band of $700–$900 / 1M tokens contingent on batching & latency settings."

Thanks — Logan
